chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called,' he said: 'If a man asks you to bear witness for him regarding a debt or a right, it is not fitting for you to decline.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on refusing to be a witness in Islamic law according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the obligation of testimony by linking it to the Quranic command not to refuse when summoned. It establishes that refusing to testify in matters of debt or rights is a neglect of a communal duty, reinforcing the legal principle that witness testimony is a collective obligation (fard kifayah) essential for establishing justice.
